raw_response:
I will still do wheat-maize on the same 3.5 mu, same as usual, because that is what fits Quzhou and my well water. On a small piece of land like mine, I do not play too many risky tricks. I watch cost, but I fear losing yield more than wasting a little fertilizer, so I will keep fertilizer a bit on the safe side. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, rotary till once after maize, put most phosphorus and potassium in the base fertilizer, split nitrogen into base plus one topdressing at jointing, and give about 2 irrigations if the field is not carrying enough moisture. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed, sow right after wheat harvest, mostly no-till or stubble seeding to save time, and I will give 1 irrigation for emergence or at big flare stage if rain does not come. I will not chase the very highest demo-plot yield, but on 3.5 mu I can manage carefully enough to aim for solid yield with 2 pesticide passes on each crop, mainly weed control plus one disease/insect control timing.
